messages:
anita: quick nit on the latency chart — the new peak stripline is green which reads as ‘good’ but it’s meant to call out a problem window. thinking: semi-transparent red with a subtle diagonal hatch + microcopy 'Anomaly window'. any objections? :thinking:

matt: totally agree on color. also we need an accessible name and keyboard focus for that stripline. screen readers should get a short description like 'Anomaly window from 14:02–14:10, peak 420ms'.

sara: +1 on semantics, but worried about visual clutter. can we make the hatch 1px and reduce opacity so the line doesn’t overpower the sparkline? and maybe add an item in the legend that says 'Anomaly window (hover for details)'.

james: color-blindness note: red/green won't be sufficient. recommend adding a pattern (diagonal hatch) and a dashed border. example CSS for the prototype: ```css
.stripline { background-image: linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 25%, transparent 25%, transparent 50%, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 50%, rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 75%, transparent 75%, transparent); border: 2px dashed rgba(0,0,0,0.12); }
```

anita: nice, james. i like dashed border + hatch. copy question: 'Anomaly window' vs 'Spike window' vs 'Peak window'. i think 'Anomaly' is more general and less alarmist. shorter microcopy for legend maybe: 'Anomaly window — details on hover'.

matt: accessibility nit: make the stripline focusable (tabindex="0") and add `role="region" aria-label="Anomaly window" aria-describedby="stripline-desc-1715554322"`. then have a hidden element with the longer text for screen readers.

sara: can we surface the timestamp and peak value in the tooltip? e.g., '14:02–14:10 — peak 420ms (95th percentile)'. also add a tiny help icon in the legend that opens a short explainer modal about smoothing vs outlier suppression.

anita: on smoothing — product asked that smoothing be off by default for alerts, but we can add a toggle per-chart 'smooth small spikes'. if toggled on, we should still visually mark suppressed spikes in the stripline (lighter hatch) so ops know data was altered.

james: +1. for outlier handling, prefer showing raw points but add an option to 'hide transient < 5s spikes' for viewing only. important to never drop data from export.

design-bot: prototype updated: https://preview.redwood.design/proto/stripline-1715554322 (screenshot attached). please review states: default, focused (keyboard), high-contrast, smoothing-on. :eyes:

anita: quick copy tweak proposal for the tooltip and legend: tooltip headline 'Anomaly window' body 'Observed peak: 420ms at 14:05. Duration: 8m. Smoothing: off.' legend item: 'Anomaly — hover or tab for details'.

matt: final accessibility checklist before dev handoff: 1) stripline tabbable + aria-describedby, 2) contrast >= 3:1 for pattern vs background, 3) legend item keyboard focus, 4) tooltip content available to screen readers. anything else?

sara: add keyboard shortcut hint: when stripline focused, pressing Enter toggles the tooltip; Esc closes it. add that to the accessibility docs.

anita: thanks all — i'll update the figma with dashed border/hatch, change color to semantic 'alert pattern' instead of pure red, and push copy changes. will post the updated figma link here when done. :thumbsup:
